requestKey: Best budgeting app for irregular income|pocketpal.me|sample1

payload.text:
Here are the budgeting apps that work best when income is irregular, and when to pick each:

- YNAB (You Need A Budget) — best overall for variable income
  - Why: zero-based “budget the money you have” method, great for living on last month’s income, robust goals/targets and credit‑card handling. Paid subscription; 34‑day trial. Pricing commonly listed around $109/year or $14.99/month—confirm at checkout. ([ynab.com](https://www.ynab.com/guide/irregular-income?utm_source=openai))

- PocketSmith — best for forward cash‑flow calendar and forecasting
  - Why: powerful day‑by‑day balance forecasts, calendar of bills/income, flexible budgeting; forecast 10 years (Premium) to 30 years (Super). Paid tiers; see plans for current pricing. ([pocketsmith.com](https://www.pocketsmith.com/tour/cash-flow-forecasts/?utm_source=openai))

- Monarch Money — best if you want modern design, joint budgeting, and rollovers
  - Why: choice of Flex or Category budgeting, rollover categories (great for seasonal or uneven months), strong connectivity and partner collaboration. Paid; typical list price shown around $99/year—verify current offer. ([help.monarchmoney.com](https://help.monarchmoney.com/hc/en-us/articles/360048883631-Budget?utm_source=openai))

- Tiller — best for percentage‑based “paycheck rules” and full customization
  - Why: auto‑feeds your bank data into Google Sheets/Excel so you can build a custom plan (e.g., 30% taxes, 20% savings, etc.) and add templates for monthly/yearly budgets and cash‑flow analysis. Paid with free trial. ([help.tiller.com](https://help.tiller.com/en/articles/3279649-what-is-tiller-and-how-does-it-work?utm_source=openai))

- Goodbudget — best lower‑cost envelope system (manual‑friendly)
  - Why: classic envelopes with optional rollover, easy for couples; Premium adds U.S. bank sync. Free tier available; Premium commonly shown at $10/month or $80/year—confirm in‑app. ([goodbudget.com](https://goodbudget.com/envelope-budgeting/?utm_source=openai))

Quick setup tips for irregular income (works with any of the above):
- Budget only money on hand; don’t plan future income until it arrives (YNAB’s core approach). ([ynab.com](https://www.ynab.com/guide/irregular-income?utm_source=openai))
- Create sinking funds/rollover categories for non‑monthly bills (insurance, taxes, holidays). In Monarch, toggle Rollovers per category; in YNAB, use targets. ([help.monarchmoney.com](https://help.monarchmoney.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411119762196-Rollover-budget-feature?utm_source=openai))
- Use a cash‑flow calendar to preview tight weeks before they happen (PocketSmith excels here). ([pocketsmith.com](https://www.pocketsmith.com/tour/cash-flow-forecasts/?utm_source=openai))
- If you’re commission/contract based, try percentage allocations per paycheck (easy to model in Tiller). ([help.tiller.com](https://help.tiller.com/en/articles/3279649-what-is-tiller-and-how-does-it-work?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me:
- your platform (iOS/Android/Web only),
- whether you budget solo or with a partner,
- and if you prefer strict envelopes vs. a flexible “left to spend” view vs. spreadsheet control,

I’ll narrow this to the single best pick and give you a 10‑minute starter setup for your situation.
